> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **152** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8c0306f5d5db836331098483902b0932dd18e6da` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

This run read `content/docs` from `008428f5a9295132562c0263c416b665043e51ca` — the merge of head `392a610a7e66af7e878647124e343c5f46958733` into base `8c0306f5d5db836331098483902b0932dd18e6da`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 008428f5a9295132562c0263c416b665043e51ca && git checkout 008428f5a9295132562c0263c416b665043e51ca
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8c0306f5d5db836331098483902b0932dd18e6da 392a610a7e66af7e878647124e343c5f46958733 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8c0306f5d5db836331098483902b0932dd18e6da && git merge --no-ff 392a610a7e66af7e878647124e343c5f46958733

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8c0306f5d5db836331098483902b0932dd18e6da
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8c0306f5d5db836331098483902b0932dd18e6da` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Round 2 — the seat's contract review (claim amendment 6418168409)

The declarations are corrected at the top of this body: **`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`**, `Metadata-protocol: none`. The published `GetTranslationsResponseSchema` accepted a body carrying `metadataForms` and now refuses it, and the exported `GetTranslationsResponse` type loses that member; nothing an author writes moves, so the kind stays `none` and the level stays `patch`.

- **The changeset carries the BREAKING banner**, the remedy (read the group from `GET /meta/types`, which serves each form already translated) and exactly one ADR-0087 disposition: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, accepted by `check-adr-0087-registration` — "1 declared-breaking changeset(s), each carrying an ADR-0087 disposition". The reason closes the other five categories on facts: both packages publish; no ADR-0087 id is named or touched; the diff touches `packages/spec/**` and a `*.zod.ts` face, which closes `type-surface-only`; the narrowed declaration is a Zod projection, which closes `runtime-interface-only`; and no export is retired. The remedy is written as prose rather than a literal `FROM → TO` label block, because that label is branch 1 of the gate's migration-prescription detector and would make the only claimable category unclaimable; the mapping it would carry ("read `metadataForms` from `GET /meta/types`") is in the changeset's "What to do" and above.
- **`requestedLocale` is now declared** on `GetTranslationsResponseSchema`, optional (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`). The door has served it on the locale-fallback exit (`zh` served as `zh-CN`) since that fallback existed, undeclared. Same schema, same class, mechanical — the in-place adjacent fix the amended claim names. Pinned on both sides: the spec test fixes the shape to `locale` / `requestedLocale` / `translations`, parses a fallback body, keeps the field optional and refuses a non-string; the runtime test parses the real fallback body against the schema.
- **Two `ui` docblocks this PR had made false are repaired.** `SPEC_TRANSLATION_GROUPS` (`ui/packages/i18n/src/utils/spec-translations.ts`) now says it is deliberately a superset of the groups the server still serves, names `metadataForms` as the first group to have left, and states the one direction that is red (a group the spec serves and the list lacks). `metadata-form-i18n.ts` (`ui/packages/app-shell`) now names `/api/v1/meta/types` as the channel that carries an environment's own `metadataForms`, and says this overlay covers the forms the console renders from its own copy of the spec.
- **`origin/main` was merged in** (merge `81dc21e7`), because editing a `ui` registry source moves that package's digest in `scripts/sdui-manifest.sources/` and `main` had just re-shaped those records one-per-package (#26120). No file in this diff overlaps `main`'s range, so the merge is textually clean. The digest was then re-recorded with the merged generator: 1 of 27 package records moved (`i18n`), `sdui.manifest.json` byte-identical at 106 components, `check-sdui-manifest` green.

Measured at the head this comment is written against, `4f5d2f0a`: the dogfood battery (closure built first, then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test` under the verify lock, no shard and no path) is `Test Files 296 passed | 3 skipped (299)`, `Tests 2523 passed | 18 skipped (2541)`, VERDICT 0. The `@objectstack/spec` suite is `803` files / `23204` tests green, the six runtime i18n files `103` tests, the type-checks clean, and the console loader plus the `@object-ui/i18n` transform suite `22` tests. The derived gate list is now 125 commands and all 125 exited 0, reconciled as "125 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED".

The declaration lines and the title of this pull request are the seat's write, not the author's (a dev writes a body once, at creation): the title takes `!` and the body's `Clause-②:` line takes `yes (narrowing)`. Until then the declaration of record for the contract review is the changeset's.
